A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and are readable throughout, including their equations, figures, tables, proofs, and experimental appendices. Reformatting and appendix reordering do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original decision-boundary analyses and classification experiments on CIFAR10-LT, CIFAR100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and Helena.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain original empirical results and add experiments combining MLA with another method and increasing class imbalance.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces reciprocal-cosine logit comparisons with a constructed boundary-normal sign test. MLA scaling and the intended angular boundaries remain unchanged. However, the revised pseudocode omits the negative beta sign required by Equation (64), so the printed procedures are not simply equivalent rewrites.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and image/tabular classification tasks. The added CIFAR experiments change class sample counts and training configurations within existing coverage; object detection and text retrieval appear only in related-work discussion.

E2.justification: New Table 11 evaluates Wang et al. (2023a) against its combination with MLA; v1 only cited that method. The original comparisons retain Baseline, ALA, 1vs1adjuster, and MLA.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds CIFAR experiments with imbalance factor 200 and a ResNet32 combination experiment using Wang et al.'s setup. The reported splits, training budgets, metrics, and hyperparameter search for the original experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F.4–F.5 add a compatibility analysis testing MLA with another augmentation method and an imbalance-sensitivity test at factor 200. Existing decision-boundary analyses and fixed-versus-tuned hyperparameter comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeded runs and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for the original accuracy experiments. Figure 3 newly repeats the already documented run count. No changed statistical procedure is reported; new Table 11 supplies point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Several 1vs1adjuster entries change in Tables 6–9; Table 7 revises its tuned average from 79.2 ± 0.8 to 79.6 ± 1.1. New Tables 11–13 add combination and stronger-imbalance results, including 44.9 versus 49.1 for Wang et al. without versus with MLA. These are added or revised results, not evidence of a same-procedure improvement between versions.

T1.justification: v3 introduces an averaged complexity term in the bounds, tightens the propositions' sample-size condition from at least two to more than two, and explicitly applies assumptions to both or all relevant classes. Appendix D adds the boundary-normal derivation. The main angular solutions and asymptotic conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the NC-based decision-boundary theory, MLA's approximation of that adjustment, empirical applicability beyond ideal assumptions, and hyperparameter guidance. Rewording the motivating question and contribution statements does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion replaces the limitation about missing complex-model experiments such as ViT with insufficient theoretical understanding of ALA; no ViT experiment is added. Appendix F adds compatibility interpretations and explicitly cautions that the Wang et al. experiment is not directly comparable with the original experiments.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly provides a code-repository address. Appendix F.4 identifies ResNet32 and adoption of Wang et al.'s implementation settings. The original hyperparameters, hardware, and data-splitting instructions were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: New Appendix B connects MLA with class-dependent temperatures, inverse image frequency, and inverse document frequency, citing Ye et al., Alexandridis et al., and Salton and Buckley. A Yang et al. survey is added, while the ViT citation is removed. The principal research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits the prose, reframes the introductory question, lists NC1–NC4 separately, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes the appendices. Explanations and captions expand, but most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into the ICLR format, changing typography, text width, headers, and placement of figures and tables. Figure 1 is revised, heatmap labels are standardized, captions expand, notation tables change, and Tables 11–13 are added.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful compatibility and imbalance tests, clearer assumptions, and code-access information. However, its revised Algorithm 1 omits the negative beta sign in Equation (64), creating a new inconsistency in the central comparison procedure. The PDFs do not establish which formulation produced the revised results. This unresolved reproducibility problem prevents a reliable net judgment against the documented gains.
